messages.content: start Docker on window using docker start.

function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a given command using the os.system() function specifically for Windows operating systems. For multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For complex tasks, create and run a .bat file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The Windows command line instruction(s) to be executed. Use '&&' between commands for multiple instructions. For complex sequences, encapsulate the logic within a .bat file and provide the execution command here.

message.reasoning:
The user says "start Docker on window using docker start." They want to start Docker on Windows using docker start. But docker start is used to start containers, not the Docker daemon. To start Docker service, you need to start the Docker Desktop or Docker Engine service. On Windows, you can use `net start com.docker.service` or `Start-Service -Name com.docker.service` via PowerShell. Or if using Docker Desktop, you can launch the Docker Desktop application.

But the user might want to start Docker engine via command line. We can use `docker-machine start default` if using Docker Machine. Or `sc start com.docker.service`. Or `Start-Service com.docker.service`.

We need to respond with a command that starts Docker service. The tool expects a Windows command line instruction. So we can give something like:

`cmd /c "sc start com.docker.service"`

Or `powershell -Command "Start-Service -Name com.docker.service"`.

We should also mention that this will start the Docker service. If Docker Desktop is installed, you can start it by launching the Docker Desktop app.

We need to output a JSON object with the command. According to the tool signature, we need to call the function with the command string. So we need to produce a JSON object with key "command" and value being the command string.

Thus we should produce:

{
  "command": "sc start com.docker.service"
}

But maybe we need to include `&&`? No, just one command.

Alternatively, we could do `cmd /c "sc start com.docker.service"`.

Better to use `sc start com.docker.service`. That will start the service.

Thus we produce the JSON.
